idiom_name: local functions capturing (and mutating) the enclosing function's variables
implementation_notes: Kotlin local functions are declared with fun inside a function body and may read and write the outer function's local vars, which is the method object's state sharing without a class. The compiler passes captured variables to a generated private method when the local function is only called directly, but a mutated captured var is boxed in a Ref wrapper and a local function used as a value becomes a synthetic class instance, so hot loops should avoid capturing mutable state. Keep the classic named class (or a data class) when the algorithm must be tested, documented as a unit, serialized, or exposed through more than one operation.
pitfalls: A local function that mutates a captured var forces the compiler to wrap that variable in a Ref object; in a loop that runs a million times those allocations add up.
Using a local function as a value (passing it to a higher-order function) allocates a synthetic FunctionN instance, while direct calls can be compiled into a private method.
Local functions must be declared before they are invoked, and nesting them more than one level deep makes the capture chain hard to follow.
